10.1002_adma.202509150: Industrial separation processes account for 10–15% of global energy consumption. Membrane‐based processes are less energy‐intensive than traditional gas separation technologies; however, enhanced material separation performance and stability for numerous gas mixtures are needed for widespread industrial adoption. This work presents a generalizable strategy for preparing mixed‐matrix gas separation membranes exceeding the performance upper bounds of existing polymer membranes for a wide variety of industrial gases. By incorporating robust porous aromatic framework (PAF) particles into various dense commercial polymer matrices, gas diffusivity and solubility can be enhanced. For diverse gas mixtures (e.g., CO 2 /N 2 , O 2 /N 2 , He/CH 4 , H 2 /N 2 , and C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 ), the resulting composite membranes exhibit enhanced gas permeabilities—by as much as 520%—and largely unchanged selectivities even after 6 years of aging under simulated flue gas conditions. These improvements arise from the ultrahigh porosity, excellent chemical compatibility, and unique physicochemical properties of the embedded PAF particles. Functionalizing the PAFs with polyamines also enables composite membranes that achieve among the highest reported performances against plasticization, a common obstacle in commercializing gas separation membranes. Significantly, the PAF‐1 particles are readily dispersible in various common membrane casting solvents, suggesting their broader utility as a filler for designing high‐performance membranes for many industrial gas separations.
10.1016_j.ocecoaman.2026.108144: Assessing multifaceted coastal risks across heterogeneous shorelines is critical for informed, long-term management. We present an index-based framework that integrates uniformly computed hazard metrics with spatially resolved exposure and vulnerability components. Our methodology decomposes overall risk into environmental, physical and socio-economic dimensions, facilitating clear area comparisons and priority setting. Applied to the 65 km long Salamanca Barrier (Colombia), a UNESCO biosphere reserve with critical infrastructure and vulnerable settlements, we divided the coast into three sectors and scored their hazard, exposure and vulnerability. The results reveal uniformly high to very high environmental risk (driven by vulnerable lagoons and rapid shoreline retreat) in west sector, moderate to high physical risk in central and eastern sectors, with a hotspot where Road 90 borders the coast, and very high socio-economic risk confined to eastern informal settlements despite lower hazard intensity. This disaggregated approach guides targeted interventions aligned with sector-specific risk profiles. While tailored to the unique values of the Salamanca Barrier, the modular design of te framework permits customization for other coastal contexts.
10.1021_acscatal.6c02814: Boron-doped copper has recently emerged as an active and stable catalyst for the electrochemical reduction of CO2 to value-added C2 products. Here, we develop a realistic model of CO electroreduction on surface borides of copper under operational conditions, taking into account the effects of electrode potential, electrolyte environment, and pH. We study the possible reconstruction of the electrocatalyst surface using grand canonical DFT and global optimization to obtain a potential-dependent grand canonical ensemble description of metastable, hydrogen-covered catalyst surfaces. Two key surface configurations, low H-coverage (LC, -0.6 VSHE) and high H-coverage (HC, -0.8 VSHE) dominate this ensemble, with the former being kinetically persistent and C2 selective under strongly reducing conditions. Nonmetallic boron sites on the surface copper boride are found to bind CO more strongly than copper sites, and mechanistic investigation of CO electroreduction pathways presents a surprisingly unconventional case of boron-centered reactivity in contrast to typical copper-centered reactivity. Neighboring boron sites present along boron chains on the surface copper boride are found to facilitate C–C coupling, thereby driving the high C2 selectivity of this electrocatalyst.
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c00803: The electrooxidation of liquid alcohols is conventionally characterized by peak-shaped voltammograms that conflate kinetic and mass-transport effects, precluding rigorous catalyst evaluation. This ambiguity stems from an unresolved competition: the hydroxide ion (OH−) is essential for reaction kinetics but, in excess, poisons the surface via rapid oxidation. Here, deliberate control of mass transport resolves this conflict, enabling the first engineering of well-defined limiting-current plateaus for methanol and ethanol oxidation. This plateau explicitly reveals an OH−-diffusion-limited regime, exposing a universal flux-activity trade-off. We leverage this insight to establish a transport-aware benchmarking framework, quantifying intrinsic activity, stability, and a new metric of flux-induced kinetic poisoning sensitivity. By balancing reactant fluxes to circumvent kinetic poisoning, an unprecedented record of geometric current density exceeding 1 A cm−2 was achieved for methanol oxidation. Our work redefines the optimization paradigm for complex electrocatalytic reactions, shifting the focus from static activity metrics to mastering dynamic interfacial flux.
